A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same conditional-learning and inverse-EOT framework. Their main text, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V4 reports original Swiss-roll experiments, weather-prediction results and neural-model experiments including colored-MNIST translation.

after.justification: V5 retains original empirical results and adds face translation, MNIST classification, quantitative synthetic evaluations and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The core GMM objective, parameterization and inference remain. V5 adds a density-ratio-weighted objective for biased pairs in Appendix B.3 and corrects Algorithm 1 by including the negative cost term on generated samples. The neural variant and finite-class extension were already described in v4.

E1.justification: V5 adds FFHQ Woman-to-Man and Old-to-Young translation in ALAE latents, ten-class MNIST classification, and an analytically generated non-OT Swiss-roll conditional scenario. These substantially extend the domains, target types and conditional relationships actually evaluated.

E2.justification: The retained Swiss-roll and weather experiments preserve their comparator line-ups. FSBM is reused for the new face tasks, and CNF (SS) denotes the existing CondNF (SS). A corrected baseline likelihood formula does not establish that a different comparator implementation was evaluated.

E3.justification: V5 introduces quantitative marginal and conditional Swiss-roll evaluation using MMD and Sinkhorn divergence, with 1024 generated samples and 30 conditioning points described in Appendix D.2. New face-metric and classification-accuracy protocols further expand evaluation. Existing Swiss-roll and weather training budgets and splits are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained source/target-data ablation, v5 adds a component-count sensitivity grid over M,N in {8,16,32,64} and MNIST labeled/unlabeled sample-count ablations. The analytical Swiss-roll experiment also probes behavior when ground truth is not generated through OT.

E5.justification: V4 reports ± values without explaining run counts or uncertainty type. V5 identifies Table 5 values as mean ± standard deviation over multiple runs and specifies three independent seeds for face comparisons. Confidence-interval-based highlighting is mentioned without defining interval construction; increased runs for retained results are not established.

E6.justification: Weather Tables 1–2 retain their values, while v5 adds substantial synthetic, face and classification results. Table 3 reports Woman-to-Man FID of 9.3±0.1 versus FSBM's 10.2±0.6; Table 5's 16k conditional MMD instead favors OTCS, 9.13±0.06 versus 35.72±0.27 for the proposed method, in units of 10^-3. The 16k OTCS visualization also changes from v4 Figure 5h to v5 Figure 6n.

T1.justification: The main propositions, approximation assumptions and Appendix E proofs are retained. V5 adds biased-pair assumptions and a weighted-objective derivation, plus metric definitions and properties. It corrects the baseline approximation from log(mean(log density)) to log(mean(density)); however, Appendix B.3's classifier odds are reciprocal to its defined density-ratio weights.

C1.justification: The central likelihood, inverse-EOT and approximation contributions remain. V5 expands the introduction and conclusion's empirical scope to classification and refines the introduction's algorithmic recovery statement into a model-class approximation claim for conditional distributions under assumptions.

C2.justification: V5 corrects the weather interpretation to acknowledge CGMM (SS)'s slightly lower CFD, 7.17 versus 7.21, while retaining the best-LL claim. It adds substantive discussions of biased-pair applicability, analytical-map failure, component-related overfitting and accuracy degradation with excessive unlabeled data.

D1.justification: Code disclosure changes from supplemental code and promised release to an explicit public-repository statement and link. V5 adds metric estimators, bandwidth selection and software settings, classification architecture details, and ALAE training settings, hardware and timing. Existing implementation details are largely retained and relocated.

R1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds substantial positioning against ground-metric learning, including Cuturi–Avis, Huizing, Auffenberg and Scarvelis–Solomon, distinguishing their objectives from conditional-coupling learning. Density-ratio, covariate-shift and evaluation literature are also added. Much of the earlier related-work discussion is relocated rather than removed.

P1.justification: V5 redistributes related work between Section 4 and Appendix B.5 and reorganizes earlier Appendices C/D into Additional Experiments and Experimental Details. Introductory and discussion passages are rewritten, explanations expanded, and EBiEOT/GMM/NN terminology introduced throughout.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, with redesigned title/author presentation, resized tables and reordered Swiss-roll panels. V5 adds face-example grids, two heatmap figures and four quantitative tables, alongside relocation and renumbering of retained displays.

improvement.justification: V5 adds valuable quantitative checks, broader experiments, reproducibility information and corrections to Algorithm 1 and the weather interpretation. However, Table 6 repeats all seven baselines' Table 5 16k conditional means and deviations as unconditional results for a different 128-pair experiment, without explanation. Appendix B.3 also reverses the classifier odds required by its defined weights. These unresolved reliability problems prevent a confident judgment of the net quality benefit.
